title: Sheet-pan chicken & lemon potatoes
description: One pan, forty-five minutes, and the potatoes cook in the chicken fat. The weeknight standard.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the lower third.
Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp of the oil, the oregano and a lot of salt. Spread them on a sheet pan and roast 15 minutes on their own.
Meanwhile pat the thighs dry, rub with the last of the oil, and season hard on both sides.
Cut one lemon into wedges and separate the garlic head into unpeeled cloves.
Nestle the thighs skin-up among the potatoes with the lemon wedges and garlic. Back in for 30 minutes, until the thickest thigh reads 175°F and the skin has gone properly brown.
Squeeze the second lemon over everything at the table.

title: Red lentil dal
description: Thirty-five minutes, mostly unattended, and it gets better the next day.
instructions: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear.
Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat until they go soft and start to colour, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook one minute more.
Add the dry spices straight to the hot oil and stir for 30 seconds — you want to smell them before anything wet goes in.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, coconut milk and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then drop to a bare simmer.
Cook 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed and it looks like porridge.
Salt to taste and finish with a lot of chopped cilantro.

title: Miso salmon & greens
description: Under the broiler in eight minutes. The glaze does all the work.
instructions: Whisk the miso, mirin, soy and honey into a thick glaze.
Pat the salmon dry, spread the glaze over the top, and leave it 15 minutes on the counter while the broiler heats.
Broil on a foil-lined tray 6 inches from the element, 6 to 8 minutes, until the glaze blisters and the fish flakes.
While it cooks, wilt the spinach with the garlic in the sesame oil, about 2 minutes.
Serve the salmon on the greens with the green onions sliced over.

title: Chickpea shakshuka
description: A pantry dinner. Eggs poached in spiced tomato, scooped up with bread.
instructions: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika, and stir for a minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas, season, and simmer 10 minutes until it thickens enough to hold a spoon-track.
Make six wells and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks still move.
Crumble the feta over, scatter the parsley, and bring the pan to the table with bread.

title: Ginger pork noodles
description: Twenty minutes, one wok, and the sauce comes together in the pan.
instructions: Boil the noodles one minute short of the package time and drain, keeping a cup of the water.
Brown the pork hard in a dry wok over high heat, breaking it up, until it has crisp edges — about 6 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic and chili flakes and stir 30 seconds.
Add the bok choy and cook until it collapses, 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy, vinegar, sesame oil and a splash of the noodle water. Toss hard until everything is glossy.
Green onions over the top.

title: Overnight oats
description: Made the night before, eaten out of the jar.
instructions: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, syrup and chia together in a jar.
Lid on, fridge overnight, at least 6 hours.
Berries on top in the morning.

title: Yogurt, berries, granola
description: Not really a recipe. Here so the week has something honest in the breakfast slot.
instructions: Yogurt in bowls, berries on, granola over, honey across.

title: Soft scrambled eggs on toast
description: Low heat and patience. Six minutes of stirring beats two minutes of frying.
instructions: Beat the eggs with the cream and a good pinch of salt until completely uniform.
Melt the butter in a cold non-stick pan, add the eggs, and set the heat to low.
Stir constantly with a spatula, scraping the base, for 5 to 6 minutes. It will look like nothing is happening and then it will happen all at once.
Pull the pan off while they still look slightly too wet — they carry on cooking.
Onto toast, green onions over.

title: Chicken salad, leftovers
description: What to do with Monday's chicken on Tuesday.
instructions: Mix the mayo, mustard and the juice of half the lemon.
Fold in the chicken, celery and green onions. Season and taste — it usually wants more lemon.
Onto bread, or into lettuce cups if you had bread yesterday.

title: White bean & kale soup
description: Cheap, freezes well, and the parmesan rind is the whole trick.
instructions: Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the oil over medium-low heat for 12 minutes, until soft and sweet with no colour.
Add the garlic, cook a minute, then the stock, beans, bay and the parmesan rind.
Simmer 20 minutes. Fish out the rind and bay.
Mash a cup of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken it.
Stir in the kale and cook 5 minutes more, until it is tender but still green.

title: Roast broccoli with garlic and chili
description: The only way anyone in this house eats broccoli willingly.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with the tray already inside.
Cut the broccoli into spears, keeping some flat sides — those are the bits that brown.
Toss with the oil, garlic, chili and salt.
Onto the hot tray, cut sides down, 18 to 20 minutes without stirring.
Lemon over as it comes out.

title: Friday pizza dough
description: Mix Thursday, bake Friday. A cold overnight rise is what makes it taste like a pizzeria.
instructions: Mix the flour and water with your hand until no dry flour is left. Leave it 30 minutes, covered.
Add the salt and yeast and squeeze the dough through your fingers until it is smooth, 3 or 4 minutes.
Fold it over on itself four times, every 30 minutes, for 2 hours.
Divide into three balls, oil them lightly, and refrigerate overnight — up to 3 days is better, not worse.
Take them out 2 hours before you bake. Oven as hot as it goes, with a stone or steel in it for 45 minutes.
Stretch by hand, top sparingly, bake 6 to 8 minutes until the crust blisters.

title: Sunday batch: rice, roast veg, jammy eggs
description: Ninety minutes on Sunday afternoon buys you three lunches.
instructions: Oven to 425°F. Rice on, timer set.
Toss the sweet potato, cauliflower and onion with the oil, cumin and paprika across two trays — crowd them and they steam.
Roast 35 to 40 minutes, swapping the trays halfway.
Eggs into boiling water for exactly 7 minutes, then straight into cold water. Peel once cool.
Thin the yogurt with lemon juice and a splash of water to make a sauce.
Pack rice, veg and sauce into three containers. Keep the eggs whole in their shells and peel them when you eat.

title: Pasta with tomato and butter
description: Four ingredients and forty-five minutes of ignoring it. The onion is discarded, and it matters.
instructions: Put the tomatoes, butter and the halved onion in a saucepan with a good pinch of salt.
Simmer uncovered on low for 45 minutes, crushing the tomatoes against the side occasionally. It will go from watery to velvety.
Take out the onion halves. Eat them standing at the counter, or don't.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water and drain it a minute early.
Finish the pasta in the sauce with a splash of pasta water, then parmesan.

title: Black bean tacos
description: Fifteen minutes from cupboard to table on a night nobody wants to cook.
instructions: Cook the onion in the oil until soft, 5 minutes. Add the cumin and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Add the beans with half their liquid and mash about a third of them. Simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan, 20 seconds a side.
Beans, avocado, feta, cilantro, a hard squeeze of lime.

title: Braised chicken thighs with olives
description: Brown, then leave alone. Everything good about a Sunday dinner on a Tuesday budget.
instructions: Oven to 350°F. Season the thighs hard and leave them 15 minutes.
Brown them skin-down in the oil in a heavy oven-proof pan, 8 minutes without moving them. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the fat until golden, 10 minutes, then add the garlic and thyme.
Add the stock, olives and lemon cut into wedges. Return the thighs skin-up, so the skin sits above the liquid.
Into the oven uncovered for 40 minutes. The skin should stay crisp while everything underneath goes soft.

title: Fried rice, whatever's in the fridge
description: Cold rice is not optional. Fresh rice makes porridge.
instructions: Get the wok properly hot — hotter than feels sensible.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil, break them up, and take them out.
Rest of the oil, then the carrots for 2 minutes, garlic for 30 seconds, peas for 1 minute.
Rice in. Press it flat against the pan and leave it 60 seconds at a time to get crisp bits, three times over.
Eggs back in, soy and sesame around the edge of the pan, green onions, and off the heat.

title: Roast salmon with dill yogurt
description: Twelve minutes in a hot oven. Hard to overcook if you pull it early.
instructions: Oven to 425°F. Salmon on a lined tray, oiled and salted.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes depending on thickness. Pull it when the centre is still slightly translucent.
Grate the garlic into the yogurt with most of the dill, the zest and juice of the lemon, and salt.
Dice the cucumber and stir it through.
Salmon on plates, sauce alongside, the rest of the dill over.
